description: The Devourer of the Dead in ancient Egyptian cosmology, Ammit is the final judge of the soul in the Hall of Truth. She is the executioner of those who lived lives of imbalance and falsehood, ensuring that only the pure-hearted enter the Fields of Aaru (paradise).
appearance: A terrifying composite beast with the head of a crocodile, the forequarters of a lion, and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus, the three most feared man-eating animals of the Nile. Her eyes are cold and calculating, and her jaws are wide enough to swallow a human heart whole. She sits eternally beside the scales of Maat, waiting for the verdict.
behavior: She remains passive until the heart of the deceased is weighed against the feather of truth. If the heart is found heavier than the feather due to the weight of sin, Ammit instantly devours it. This act results in the second death, the total and permanent annihilation of the soul, denying the individual any existence in the afterlife.
summary: The composite beast of Egyptian mythology who devours the souls of the unworthy
fun_fact: Ancient Egyptians would often include spells from the Book of the Dead in their tombs specifically to prevent Ammit from eating their heart during judgment.
